newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Evergo takes stake in Shanghai property.
newsitem.headline: Evergo takes stake in Shanghai property.

text.p: Evergo China Holdings Ltd, a subsidiary of Chinese Estates Holdings Ltd, will acquire an interest in a property development project in Shanghai, the company said.
The acquisition will be financed mostly by a new share issue.
Evergo will acquire a 35 percent stake in Grand Make International Ltd in two separate acquisitions, the company said in an announcement published on Monday.

Grand Make holds 99 percent of the Shanghai property which comprises a hotel, offices, service apartments, and retail premises in a total of 61 floors, including three basement floors. Site clearance work on the property has been completed, the notice said.
The remaining one percent is held by Shanghai Luwan Area Construction Development Co, a government-owned company, it said.

Following the acquisitions and based on existing shareholdings, New World China will hold 45 percent of the issued capital of and loans to Grand Make, Evergo will hold 35 percent and three independent third parties will hold the remaining 20 percent, the announcement said.
Evergo's major shareholder, Chinese Estates, will place 240 million shares of its existing holding to independent parties, then subscribe for 240 million new shares at the new placement price.

The shares are to be placed at HK$1.09 per share, which represents a discount of about 7.60 percent to the closing price per share of HK$1.18 of Evergo on May 14. Placing will be completed on Wednesday.

The new shares will represent 16.67 percent of the company's enlarged issued capital and will reduce the holding of Chinese Estates to 53.19 percent from 63.82 percent, the notice said. However, if the subscription of new shares does not proceed, Chinese Estates' shareholding will fall to 43.82 percent.

The net proceeds from the subscription of new shares are estimated at HK$253 million. The total cost of the acquisition of the stake in the Shanghai property amounts to HK$280.47 million. The balance of the consideration not covered by the new share issue will be funded from internal resources, it said.
An application has been made to the stock exchange for a waiver of the requirement for shareholder approval of the acquisitions, the announcement said.
